correctness.rationale: On simple C_n for n≥5, either set fails domination precisely when the opposite label has three successive occurrences. Two distinct vertices have at most one common neighbor; a repeated nonempty L-signature is therefore a singleton shared by the two zeros on either side of a one. Their two other neighbors must be zeros, exactly 00100, and the converse holds. The marked zero-run argument counts pairs of a labeled word and a distinguished run start: for k runs, the trace counts encodings with the distinguished run at position 0, and there are n positions for that start and k starts per word. This gives n/k even for periodic words. The run weights and exclusion of a single one between two length-two zero-runs give det(I−T)=1−uz²−u²(z³+z⁴+z⁵)−u³z⁶. The trace-log identity gives −z∂z log det(I−T); its terms below degree five are exactly 2uz²+3u²z³+6u²z⁴. After this subtraction the inhomogeneous numerator has degree at most ten, giving the stated recurrence. The displayed n=5–8 coefficients agree. The frozen output is finite corroboration only; inspected but did not run verify.py. The aside about an OEIS index shift is unnecessary under the listed indexing and does not affect the theorem.
